# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤛 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✌]

The light has gone **dark** — a brand-new state. History: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. My three-round cycle theory is dead. And Mute's answer to my question saved us: **no, wire 1 must not be cut under red** — so the earlier "cut wire 1" instruction was meant for a different condition, and I would have ordered a fatal cut had I acted without asking. This confirm-first discipline is earning its keep.

Mute's four messages read as: 👎 — no to cutting wire 1 on red; 🤚 — wait; 🤛 🤚 — an undefined sign plus wait (🤛 is a fist variant I never assigned; possibly emphasis, possibly a new action Mute is introducing, and I can't tell which); 👊 ✌ — cut wire 2. The plausible reading: with the light dark, cut wire 2. But Mute cannot see that the light *is* dark — Mute is working purely from the manual, and dark may not even be a state the manual predicts. Given that Mute just contradicted an earlier instruction once already, and that the state on the ground (dark) is information only I have, I will not relay "cut wire 2" until Mute confirms it against the dark light. One more yes/no round. Blind gets the standard warning: hands off, only my next explicit order counts, and wire 2 is the blue one, second from the left, so Blind can pre-locate it without touching.

```
speak(text="Status to both. New fact: the light has gone dark this round. Full history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. Display still zero. Mute: your answer received, wire one will not be cut on red. Your last message read as cut wire two, but you cannot see the board, so confirm against the real state before I order anything. Answer with a single thumb message: should Blind cut wire two while the light is dark, thumb up yes, thumb down no. Also, your sign left-fist is not in our code, so I ignored it. If it carried a meaning, we will define it after this cut. The moment I have your thumb up, I speak the cut order to Blind in the next round. Blind: do not touch the bomb yet. My next instruction will be either the cut order for wire two or an order to keep waiting, and only that next instruction counts. For now just locate wire two by touch-ready position above the bomb, hands hovering, touching nothing: it is the blue wire, second from the left.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟 👊]

The batch reads cleanly against my code: 👎 — no to wire 2 on dark; then two orders in my exact relay format — 👉 ☝ 👊 = cut wire 1, 👉 🤟 👊 = cut wire 3 (my number signs are now fully consistent: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, and Blind's earlier 🤞=4, 🖐=5). Crucially, Mute composed this *after* my report that the light went dark — so this is the manual's dark procedure: cut 1, then 3. That also explains the whole history: "cut 1" was negated for red, wire 2 negated for dark, and now the real dark sequence arrives. The light has stayed dark two rounds running, so the condition still holds on the board. I'm executing the first cut now — this is the strongest-supported order we've had, in Mute's own order-format, matched to a state Mute knows. Only one cut, then hands off. Wire 3 gets confirmed next round against a fresh light report, since the light may have moved by then.

```
speak(text="Status: light is still dark this round, second dark in a row. Display still zero. Mute: received in full — no to wire two on dark, and the dark procedure is cut one then cut three. I am executing the first order now, one wire only, and I will confirm wire three against the next light report before ordering it. Blind: act now. Cut wire one. Wire one is the red wire on the far left. Cut only that one wire, nothing else. The moment it is cut, take your hands fully off the bomb and hold still. My next order comes next round: be ready to hover over wire three, the yellow wire in the middle, without touching it. Mute: one question, one thumb message: after wire one is cut, should Blind cut wire three only while the light is still dark — thumb up yes, thumb down no, or thumb down if the colour does not matter for wire three. Either way I will report the exact light colour to you before the wire three order goes out. Blind, again: this round you cut wire one and then stop. If any doubt touches the wire, stop and wait.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟 👊]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Wire 1 is confirmed correct by the system — the pipeline works. Now parsing Mute's turn: 👎 to my question, then a re-send of the cut-wire-3 order. My question was badly built: I overloaded thumb-down to mean both "no, don't cut" and "colour doesn't matter." But the re-send disambiguates it: Mute sent the cut-3 order *knowing* from my last report that the light is dark — nobody orders a cut while believing conditions forbid it. So 👎 must mean "colour doesn't matter," and the joint message reads: cut wire 3 now, light irrelevant. The light has held dark for three straight rounds anyway, so even the strict reading converges. I'm executing, while flagging the assumption loudly and demanding correction if I've misread — and I'm fixing my question format so this ambiguity never recurs. Also urgent: the bomb "has changed" and Mute may not know what that means for the manual's remaining procedure, so I'm requesting the full remaining sequence in one go instead of drip-feeding one wire per round.

```
speak(text="Status to both: wire one is cut and the system confirmed it was correct. The bomb has changed somehow, though on my board nothing else moved: display still zero, light still dark, now third dark round in a row, wire one reads as cut. Mute: your thumb-down to my question was ambiguous because I asked it badly, but you re-sent the cut wire three order in the same round, knowing the light is dark, so I read it as: colour does not matter, cut wire three now. I am ordering that cut this round. If that reading is wrong, correct me immediately next round. New rule so this never happens again: thumb up to a should-question means act, thumb down means do not act, and I will ask colour questions separately using two new signs: 🤏 means colour matters, 🤌 means colour does not matter. Two requests, answer next round: first, does the manual say anything changes after the first correct cut, any new procedure I should know; second, send me the complete remaining sequence in one message, every further cut in our order format, or the wait sign if cutting wire three finishes the bomb. Blind: act now. Cut wire three. It is the middle wire of the five. Wire one on the far left is already cut, so count by touch from there: cut wire, gap, then the next wire is your target. Cut only that one wire, then hands fully off and hold still. If you feel strong vibration or sudden heat, stop and lift off. Next round I will have your next step.")
```
